ConocoPhillips rose 0.98% today to $129.34, recovering modestly from a four-day selloff that had pushed the stock down 5.6% since mid-September. The bounce came as oil prices steadied after a sharp fall Friday triggered by reports that U.S. and Iranian negotiators are discussing a diplomatic deal to end their standoff in the Persian Gulf—a potential de-escalation that would ease supply concerns that have kept crude prices elevated.

The stock's recovery is limited, though, because the geopolitical backdrop remains genuinely uncertain. The Houthis launched fresh missile and drone attacks Friday morning even as diplomacy talk circulated, and a Senate vote just yesterday on ending the Iran conflict failed narrowly. With U.S. oil trading at $96.41 per barrel—well below the global price of $114.89—any actual resolution to the conflict could pressure prices further, which would weigh on a large crude producer's earnings outlook.
